description: The FXI alphabet: every code an FXI string may contain, by layer. Closed within a rules revision: a code not listed here makes the string invalid. A later rules revision of the same major may only add codes or split a code into children.

layers.description: Motion: the joint actions of each phase, in rep order. Required.
Orientation: the body to gravity at the start of the rep. Always written; `?` if unknown.
Moving end, for trunk work on the floor or a bench. Default: the limb end moves.
Footwork: stepping, split stance or travel. Default: feet planted level.
Support: surfaces beyond what the orientation implies, and the body points on them. Default: the floor as the orientation implies.
Load: each implement and where it is held, or `bw`. Always written; `?` if unknown.
Symmetry: which limbs work and in what order. Default: `b`, both together.
Grip and stance: hand orientation, width, stance. Default: the usual grip, medium width, medium stance.
Range and start: partial or deep range, deficit, start position. Default: full range from the usual start.
Held posture of limbs that do not work. Default: no held posture.
Line of pull or path past the body. Default: the line the movement word implies.
Accessory: a strap or a partner that helps the exercise without loading it. Extended: compared only when both strings carry it.

joints.description: Joints a joint action names. A joint that circles takes the `.circ` action; `<joint>.?` is a joint that moves in an unknown direction.

entries.description: Neck.
Spine: the trunk, thoracic and lumbar together.
Scapula: the shoulder blade on the rib cage.
Shoulder joint.
Elbow.
Forearm: the turn that rotates the palm.
Wrist.
Hip.
Knee.
Ankle and foot.

jointActions.description: Joint actions, written `<joint>.<action>`. Two opposite actions never share one part of a phase.

entries.description: Neck flexion: chin toward the chest.
Neck extension: head tips back.
Neck side bend: ear toward the shoulder.
Neck rotation: turning the head.
Trunk flexion: ribs toward the pelvis, as in a crunch.
Trunk extension: straightening or arching the back from a bent position.
Trunk side bend.
Trunk rotation: shoulders twist against the hips.
Scapular elevation: shrug up.
Scapular depression: shoulders pulled down.
Scapular protraction: shoulder blades spread around the ribs.
Scapular retraction: shoulder blades squeezed together.
Shoulder flexion: arm forward and up, as in a front raise or overhead press.
Shoulder extension: arm down and back from in front, as in a row or a dip. Covers `sh.ext.oh`.
Shoulder extension from overhead: the arms come down in front of the face from above the head, as in a chin-up, a close or neutral pulldown, a straight-arm pulldown, a pullover or a slam.
Shoulder abduction: arm out to the side and up, as in a lateral raise.
Shoulder adduction: arm down to the side from out to the side, as in a wide pull-up.
Horizontal adduction: arm across the front at chest height, as in a press or fly.
Horizontal abduction: arm back and out at chest height, as in a reverse fly.
Shoulder internal rotation: forearm turns in toward the belly, elbow bent.
Shoulder external rotation: forearm turns out, elbow bent.
Elbow flexion, as in a curl.
Elbow extension, as in a press or triceps extension.
Forearm pronation: palm turns down.
Forearm supination: palm turns up.
Wrist flexion: palm toward the forearm.
Wrist extension: back of the hand toward the forearm.
Wrist radial deviation: thumb side toward the forearm.
Wrist ulnar deviation: little-finger side toward the forearm.
Hip flexion: thigh toward the trunk, or trunk toward the thigh.
Hip extension: thigh away from the trunk, as in standing up from a squat.
Hip abduction: leg out to the side.
Hip adduction: leg in toward the other leg.
Hip internal rotation: knee turns in.
Hip external rotation: knee turns out.
Knee flexion against resistance, as in a leg curl.
Knee extension, as in standing up from a squat.
Ankle dorsiflexion: toes toward the shin.
Ankle plantar flexion: rising onto the toes, pushing off.
Ankle inversion: sole turns in.
Ankle eversion: sole turns out.

phasePrefixes.description: The kind of a motion part, written before its actions. The empty prefix is a normal moving phase.

entries.description: Dynamic: the joints move through range; write the concentric direction.
Ballistic: the phase ends in flight (body leaves the ground) or release (implement leaves the hands). A phase after it happens in the air.
Cyclic: continuous cycles with no rep boundary; write the driving half of one cycle.
Isometric: a hold under effort for the whole set; write what the muscles push toward. `=0` is a hold with no direction (balance).
Static stretch: the directions the joints are taken to, held at end range.
Dynamic stretch: the same directions, taken to end range and released repeatedly (swings, pass-throughs).

orientations.description: The body to gravity at the start of the rep. `impliedPoints` are the body points the orientation already puts on its support; they are never written in `s`.

entries.description: On the feet, trunk within about 30° of vertical.
On the feet, trunk hinged forward more than about 30° and held there (bent-over row).
Sitting, trunk more than 60° from horizontal.
Sitting, trunk hinged forward over the thighs and held there (seated bent-over raise).
On both knees, trunk upright. On hands and knees is `prone`.
On one knee, the other foot forward.
Face up, trunk within 15° of horizontal.
Face up, head higher than hips, trunk 15–60° from horizontal.
Face up, head lower than hips, trunk 15–60° from horizontal.
Face down, trunk within 15° of horizontal: lying, plank, push-up, on hands and knees.
Face down, head higher than hips, 15–60° (hands raised).
Face down, head lower than hips, 15–60° (feet raised).
Face down, hips highest, hands and feet down, trunk more than 60° head-down (pike).
On one side: lying, or a side plank.
Held up by the hands or arms, feet off the floor: hanging from a bar, propped on dip bars.
Upside down, trunk within 30° of vertical, head lowest: handstand, headstand.

movingEnds.description: Which end of the body moves.

entries.description: The limb end moves (default, never written).
The trunk end moves; the legs stay put: sit-up, crunch, bridge, hip thrust, back extension, glute-ham raise, Nordic curl.
Both ends move toward each other: V-up, jackknife, tuck-up.
Feet planted level (default). Written only inside a sequence.
Feet planted in a split stance, one in front of the other.
Each rep steps forward and returns.
Each rep steps back and returns.
Each rep steps to the side and returns.
Each rep steps back and across behind the other leg (curtsy) and returns.
The body travels forward and does not return each rep.
Travels backward.
Travels sideways.

bodyPoints.description: Body points: where an implement is held (`l`) and which points bear weight on a support (`s`).

entries.description: The hands, or one hand.
The forearms, elbows bent (elbow plank).
The crook of the elbows (Zercher).
The upper arms (preacher pad).
On the front of the shoulders and collarbones (front rack), or on one shoulder.
Against the chest (goblet, bear hug).
Across the upper back (back squat).
Across the front of the hips (hip thrust).
Hung from a belt at the waist.
The buttocks (sitting down onto a box or bench).
On or around the thighs.
At or around the knees.
The shins.
The calves (the back of the lower leg).
At or just above the ankles (strap, cuff, machine pad on the lower leg).
The feet, or one foot.
The head or forehead.

holdOnlyPoints.description: Hold points that are not body points; written after `@` in `l` only.

entries.description: Held in the hands with the arms straight overhead for the whole rep.
The implement takes part of the body weight (assist band, assisted machine).

symmetry.description: Which limbs work and in what order.

entries.description: Bilateral: both limbs work together, or the movement has no sides (default, never written).
Unilateral: one side does every rep of the set, then the other side.
Alternating: the sides take turns rep by rep; one side works while the other waits.
Reciprocal: both sides move at once in opposite directions (gait, flutter kicks, see-saw press).

symmetryScopes.description: The limbs a symmetry code applies to, written after `@`.

entries.description: The pattern applies to the arms.
The pattern applies to the legs.

handOrientations.description: Hand orientation. The usual one is `su` when every action is `el.flex`, `pr` otherwise; a trap bar forces `ne`.

entries.description: Pronated: palms down or away (overhand).
Supinated: palms up or toward you (underhand).
Neutral: palms face each other (hammer).
Mixed: one hand over, one under.

gripWidths.description: Grip width, for hands on an implement or on a support.

entries.description: Hands touching or overlapping (diamond).
Narrow: hands inside shoulder width.
Medium: about shoulder width (default, never written).
Wide: hands well outside shoulder width.

stances.description: Stance width; written only for a standing start, or feet on a machine foot plate.

entries.description: Narrow stance: feet together or closer than hip width.
Medium stance: about hip width (default, never written).
Wide stance (sumo).

ranges.description: Range and start codes. At most one start code; `partial` and `deep` contradict. A child refines its parent.

entries.description: Part of the usual range on purpose: half, quarter, pulses, top or bottom half.
Deeper than the usual range: full depth, ass to grass, pistol depth.
Standing on something to go deeper than usual.
Each rep starts with the load at rest on the floor, where the usual start is not the floor.
Starts standing with the load held, lowered without being set down (hang), where that is not the usual start. With no child, the usual hang: above the knee.
A hang that starts at or below the knee. Child of `from-top`.
Each rep starts from pins, blocks or a rack above the floor.
Each rep starts with a drop: the body steps off a box or platform and lands before the working phase (depth jump). The box dropped from is not written in `s`.

heldPostures.description: Held posture of limbs that do not work.

entries.description: No held posture: the non-working limbs do what the movement word implies (default, never written).
Arms held straight overhead, nothing in the hands.
Arms held straight and reaching forward from the shoulders, nothing in the hands ("arms extended", "straight arm").
Arms held out to the sides.
Arms crossed on the chest.
Hands behind or on the head (prisoner).
Working elbows held bent at about 90° ("bent arm", "90 degree").
Upper arms held up beside the head while the elbows work (overhead triceps extension).
Upper arms held out from the sides, elbows flared, while the elbows work (inner biceps curl, Tate press).
Free leg held straight in front.
Free leg held behind.
Legs held straight at about 90° hip flexion.
Knees held bent while the hips or arms work (hanging knee raise; inverted row with the feet flat on the floor).
Trunk held leaning forward where the orientation does not already say so (chest dip).

lines.description: Line of pull, or the path of the load past the body.

entries.description: The line of pull the movement word implies (default, never written).
Cable or band anchored higher than usual for the movement word.
Anchored lower than usual for the movement word.
The load or the body passes behind the head or trunk instead of in front (behind-the-neck press, rear pull-up).
The load pulls from one side: the body stands side-on to the anchor (a cable press done side-on).
The load comes down to the neck, throat or chin instead of the chest (JM press, guillotine press).
A rope passes under the feet twice in each jump (double under).

accessories.description: Accessories that help the exercise without loading or supporting it. Extended layer.

entries.description: No accessory (default, never written).
A strap, belt, towel or rope used to pull or hold a limb (stretching strap).
A partner who holds, resists or assists.

equipmentTokens.description: Equipment tokens. Each is an alias of one standard FXE (`fxe`). A token with `load: true` may appear in `l`; a token with `support: true` may appear in `s`. A child refines its parent.
